key_insight: The paper introduces a hardware-safety gate that lets an LLM write native ARTIQ control code for trapped-ion experiments only when each hardware action is explicitly authorized by a token tied to its exact contents.
engineering_relevance: This creates a practical path to safer autonomous lab control by separating agent-generated decisions from hardware execution with per-operation bounds and human approval for sensitive actions.
method: LLM agent writes experimental control scripts through an MCP server to the existing ARTIQ stack.
Tokens are issued either by checking proposed scripts in an isolated hardware simulation against device-specific safety bounds or by manual human authorization.
Unauthorized or adversarial tool calls are blocked unless they match a valid token bound to the exact request.
evidence_signal: The system was demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform by autonomously building a full calibration stack, closing a magnetic-field-stabilization loop with operator guidance, and confirming portability on a second $^{171}$Yb$^{+}$ system.
watch_item: The protection boundary is precise but not complete, so adversarial scripts reveal where stronger safeguards are still needed, especially for metacognitive failures and problem re-framing.
paper_title: A hardware-safety-gated system for LLM-written native ARTIQ control code on a trapped-ion platform
